old_caption:
The video begins with a serene view of a forested area, where a wide, open field stretches between two dense lines of trees. The sky is overcast, casting a soft, diffused light over the scene. The ground appears dry and slightly uneven, with some patches of grass and dirt visible.

A bright flash of light erupts from the center of the field, accompanied by a burst of sparks and debris. This creates a dramatic contrast against the muted colors of the surroundings. The ejection is a continuous, sustained event forming a tall, expanding column of dark, fragmented matter with intermittent glowing embers. A cloud of smoke billows and expands from the base as the main event progresses. The camera appears to be moving slightly, as the perspective shifts subtly over time. The surrounding trees remain upright and unmoved, though the force of the ejection causes visible disturbance to the ground and surrounding area.
original_wisa_caption:
The video begins with a serene view of a forested area, where a wide, open field stretches between two dense lines of trees. The sky is overcast, casting a soft, diffused light over the scene. The ground appears dry and slightly uneven, with some patches of grass and dirt visible.

Suddenly, a bright flash of light erupts from the center of the field, accompanied by a burst of sparks and debris. This explosion creates a dramatic contrast against the muted colors of the surroundings. As the initial shockwave subsides, a cloud of smoke rises from the impact site, gradually dispersing into the air. The surrounding trees remain stationary, their green foliage undisturbed except for the slight movement caused by the explosion's force. The camera remains static throughout, capturing the entire sequence without any noticeable panning or zooming, allowing viewers to focus on the explosive event and its immediate aftermath.
caption:
A static outdoor view shows a forest clearing with a dirt track receding toward the horizon, flanked by pine trees under a grey overcast sky. At the center sits a dark mound of earth, with a thin cable lying to its left. A vertical column of dark debris is already being thrown upward from the mound.

Near the top of the column a bright orange-yellow glowing ball rises steadily and exits the upper edge of the scene. Red and orange sparks fill the mid-section for a moment before diminishing. As the ejection continues, the tight vertical jet widens and elongates into a broad, tall fan of scattered dark dots that spreads across much of the sky. A faint white smoke cloud at the base of the mound grows into a larger billowing plume that lingers around it. The trees, track, cable and the two small blocks in the lower-right corner appear fixed throughout, with no apparent camera motion.

This is a TEMPORALLY CROPPED EXCERPT from a longer video, not a complete event or a loop.
The first view may already be mid-action; the last view need not contain completion. Different
endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.
Do not shorten a rich caption into a terse technical checklist. Avoid annotation phrases such as
'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.

must actually correct the cited issue. This is a fallible automatic review, not proof of correctness.
